solution: n. A method for solving a problem or dealing with a difficult situation; in a scientific context, a liquid mixture in which the minor component (the solute) is uniformly distributed within the major component (the solvent).
sophisticated: adj. Developed to a high degree of complexity and refinement; having or showing a great deal of worldly experience and knowledge of fashion and culture.
source: n. A place, person, or thing from which something originates or can be obtained.
sovereign: adj. Possessing supreme or ultimate power; acting or done independently and without outside interference, especially in the context of a state or its governing body.
sparse: adj. Small in number or amount and spread out over a large area; thinly dispersed or scattered.
specialist: n. A person who concentrates primarily on a particular subject or activity; a person highly skilled in a specific and restricted field.
specialization: n. The process of concentrating on and becoming an expert in a particular subject or skill, often leading to greater efficiency and knowledge in a narrow field.
specific: adj. Clearly defined or identified; relating to a particular and exact thing, rather than something general.
specify: v. To identify or state something clearly and definitely.
spectacular: adj. Extremely impressive, beautiful, or dramatic, often on a large scale, attracting public attention.
spectrum: n. A continuous sequence or range, such as the band of colors produced when light is dispersed by a prism, or more broadly, a wide range of related ideas, qualities, or conditions.
speculate: v. To form a theory or conjecture about a subject without firm evidence.
splendour: n. Great beauty and impressive appearance; magnificence.
spore: n. A minute, typically one-celled, reproductive unit capable of giving rise to a new individual without sexual fusion, characteristic of lower plants, fungi, and protozoans.
stability: n. The state of being resistant to change, disruption, or motion; the quality of being firm, steady, and not likely to fall or be overthrown.
stagnant: adj. Characterized by a lack of activity, growth, or development; not advancing or progressing.
stagnation: n. A state of inactivity, a lack of development, growth, or progress.
standard: n. A level of quality or attainment used as a measure, norm, or model in comparative evaluations.
stature: n. The level of respect, importance, or reputation that someone or something has achieved, often in a particular field or community.
statutory: adj. Required, permitted, or enacted by a statute, which is a formal written law passed by a legislative body.
steadily: adv. In a regular and unwavering manner; continuously and at an even, predictable pace.
stealthily: adv. In a cautious and surreptitious manner, so as not to be seen or heard.
stem: v. To originate in or be caused by; to have something as its origin or main cause.
stereotype: n. A widely held but fixed and oversimplified image or idea of a particular type of person or thing.
sterilize: v. To make something free from bacteria or other living microorganisms.
stipulate: v. To demand or specify a requirement, typically as part of a bargain or agreement.
strain: n. A specific genetic variant or subtype of a microorganism, such as a bacterium or virus; also, a force or pressure tending to pull or stretch something to an extreme or damaging degree.
strew: v. To scatter or spread things untidily over a surface or area.
subconscious: adj. Relating to the part of the mind of which one is not fully aware but which influences one's actions and feelings.
submissive: adj. Ready to conform to the authority or will of others; meekly obedient or passive.
submit: v. To present a proposal, application, or other document to a person or body for consideration or judgment; or to yield to a superior force or to the authority or will of another person.
subsequent: adj. Coming after something in time; following.
subsidize: v. To support an organization or activity financially; to pay part of the cost of something, usually to reduce prices for the buyer.
substance: n. A particular kind of matter with uniform properties; also, the essential or most important part of something.
substitution: n. The action of replacing someone or something with another person or thing.
substratum: n. A layer that lies underneath another; a foundation or basis on which something is built or develops, used in fields like linguistics, geology, and biology.
subtle: adj. Not obvious, and therefore difficult to notice, understand, or describe; characterized by fine or delicate distinctions.
subversive: adj. Tending or intended to undermine the power and authority of an established system or institution.
succinct: adj. Briefly and clearly expressed; using few words to state or express an idea.
sufficient: adj. As much as is needed; enough for a particular purpose.
sufficiently: adv. To a degree that is adequate or enough for a particular purpose.
suffrage: n. The right to vote in political elections.
sullen: adj. Bad-tempered and sulky; gloomy and resentfully silent.
summon: v. To officially order someone to be present, especially for a legal or official purpose; to call people together for a meeting; to gather or call upon a quality or strength from within oneself.
superficial: adj. Concerned only with what is obvious or on the surface; not thorough, deep, or complete.
superficially: adv. In a way that is not thorough, deep, or complete; on the surface only.
supersede: v. To take the place of something or someone previously in authority or use; to replace it because it is more modern or effective.
supplant: v. To take the place of and serve as a substitute for, especially by force, strategy, or superiority.
supplement: n. Something that completes or enhances something else when added to it, often used in the context of diet, publications, or finance.
suppress: v. To prevent something from being expressed, seen, or from developing, often by force or authority.
surge: v. To increase suddenly and powerfully, often like a wave.
surgical: adj. Relating to or used in surgery; characterized by extreme precision, accuracy, and care, as if performed by a surgeon.
surveillance: n. The close observation of a person or group, especially one under suspicion, or the monitoring of behavior, activities, or data for the purpose of influencing, managing, or protecting.
survey: n. An investigation into the opinions, behavior, or characteristics of a particular group of people by asking a series of questions.
sustain: v. To cause or allow something to continue for a period of time; to keep alive or in existence.
sustainable: adj. Able to be maintained at a certain rate or level, particularly in a way that avoids the depletion of natural resources to support long-term ecological balance.
synthesis: n. The combination of components or elements to form a connected whole, either through a chemical reaction or the integration of ideas.
tackle: v. To make determined efforts to deal with a difficult problem or task.
tamper: v. To interfere with something in order to cause damage or make unauthorized alterations.
tariff: n. A tax or duty to be paid on a particular class of imports or exports.
technique: n. A particular way of carrying out a task, especially the execution or performance of an artistic work or a scientific procedure that requires special skill.
teem: v. To be full of or swarming with; to be present in large numbers.
telepathic: adj. Relating to or having the supposed ability to communicate with another person's mind without using speech, writing, or any other normal method of communication.
telltale: adj. Revealing or indicating something that was meant to be secret or is not immediately obvious.
tenacious: adj. Not readily relinquishing a position, principle, or course of action; determined and persistent.
tendency: n. An inclination or predisposition toward a particular characteristic, action, or type of behavior.
tentative: adj. Not certain or fixed; provisional; done without confidence or with hesitation.
tentatively: adv. In a way that is not certain or definite; subject to further confirmation or change.
terminate: v. To bring to an end or cause to end, often in a formal or official capacity.
territory: n. An area of land under the jurisdiction of a ruler or state; it can also refer to an area defended by an animal or group of animals, or a subject or area of activity that someone has knowledge of or responsibility for.
theory: n. A well-substantiated explanation of some aspect of the natural or social world, based on a body of facts that have been repeatedly confirmed through observation and experiment.
thereby: adv. As a result of that action or event; by that means.
thoroughly: adv. In a complete and careful way, with great attention to every detail.
threat: n. A person or thing likely to cause damage or danger; a declaration of an intention to inflict harm.
threshold: n. The level or point at which something starts to happen or take effect, often referring to the minimum intensity of a stimulus needed to produce a sensation or a response.
thrust: v. To push suddenly and forcefully in a particular direction; to exert a continuous propulsive force.
toxic: adj. Containing or being poisonous material, especially when capable of causing death or serious debilitation; can also refer to something extremely harsh, malicious, or harmful in a figurative sense.
toxin: n. A poisonous substance of a kind produced by living cells or organisms; a poison of plant or animal origin.
tragedy: n. An event causing great suffering, destruction, and distress, such as a serious accident, crime, or natural catastrophe; also, a genre of drama based on human suffering that invokes catharsis in its audience.
transaction: n. An agreement, communication, or movement carried out between separate entities or people, often involving the exchange of items of value, such as goods, services, or money.
transform: v. To make a thorough or dramatic change in the form, appearance, or character of something or someone.
transmit: v. To cause something, such as a disease, information, or energy, to pass on from one person, place, or thing to another.
transparent: adj. (of a process, system, or statement) easy to perceive or detect; open to public scrutiny; readily understood.
transplant: v. To move an organ, tissue, or living thing from one body or place to another.
treaty: n. A formally concluded and ratified agreement between sovereign states or international organizations.
tremendous: adj. Extremely large in scale, amount, or intensity; exceptionally great.
tripe: n. The first or second stomach of a ruminant, such as a cow, used as food; also, informally, something considered worthless or of poor quality; nonsense.
tyranny: n. Cruel, unreasonable, or arbitrary use of power or control; a government in which a single ruler is vested with absolute power.
tyrant: n. A cruel and oppressive ruler who holds absolute power, often having seized it illegally or unconstitutionally.
unanimously: adv. In a way that is fully in agreement; with the agreement of all people involved.
unbiased: adj. Not influenced by personal feelings or opinions in considering and representing facts; impartial.
unconscious: adj. In a state lacking awareness and the capacity for sensory perception; or, referring to mental processes occurring without the subject's awareness.
undergo: v. To experience or be subjected to something, typically something that involves a change or is unpleasant.
underlie: v. To be a cause or basis of something, often in a way that is not immediately obvious.
undermine: v. To lessen the effectiveness, power, or ability of, especially gradually or insidiously.
undertake: v. To commit oneself to and begin a task or enterprise, especially one that is large or difficult.
unify: v. To bring or join together into a single, cohesive whole; to make or become one.
unique: adj. Being the only one of its kind; unlike anything else.
unite: v. To join together for a common purpose or to make into a single unit.
unity: n. The state of being joined as a whole, or the quality of being one in spirit, purpose, or action.
uphold: v. To confirm, support, or maintain a principle, decision, or law, especially when it is being challenged.
uptake: n. The action of taking in or absorbing a substance, such as by a living organism; or, the rate of acceptance or adoption of a new idea, product, or technology.
urbanity: n. The quality of being suave, courteous, and refined in manner; the characteristic of being elegant and sophisticated, often associated with city life.
urbanization: n. The process by which an increasing proportion of a population lives in cities and suburbs, often linked to economic and social changes like industrialization.
utilize: v. To make practical and effective use of something, often a resource or opportunity, for a particular purpose.
vague: adj. Not clearly or explicitly stated or expressed; not having a precise meaning.
valid: adj. Having a sound basis in logic or fact; reasonable or cogent. Legally or officially acceptable.
validity: n. The quality of being logically or factually sound; the state of being legally or officially binding or acceptable.
vaporize: v. To convert or be converted into a gaseous state, typically by the application of heat.
venture: n. A business enterprise or project, typically a new one, that involves risk or uncertainty.
verify: v. To make sure or demonstrate that something is true, accurate, or justified.
versatile: adj. Able to adapt or be adapted to many different functions or activities.
versatility: n. The quality of being able to adapt or be adapted to many different functions or activities.
vertebrate: n. An animal of a large group distinguished by the possession of a backbone or spinal column, including mammals, birds, reptiles, amphibians, and fishes.
viable: adj. Capable of working, functioning, or developing successfully; having a reasonable chance of succeeding.
vicinity: n. The area near or surrounding a particular place.
vigorously: adv. In a way that involves physical strength, effort, or energy; strenuously.
violate: v. To break or fail to comply with a formal agreement, rule, or law; to treat something with disrespect or to disturb it.
violation: n. An action that breaks or acts against something, especially a law, agreement, principle, or something that should be treated with respect.
virtually: adv. In effect or essence, though not in fact or name; almost or nearly.
vital: adj. Absolutely necessary or important; essential for the continuation of life or the success of something.
vitality: n. The state of being strong, active, and full of energy; the power giving continuance of life, present in all living things.
volatile: adj. Liable to change rapidly and unpredictably, especially for the worse; (of a substance) easily evaporated at normal temperatures.
voracious: adj. Wanting or devouring great quantities of food; having a very eager approach to an activity.
vulnerable: adj. Susceptible to physical or emotional attack or harm; exposed to the possibility of being attacked or harmed.
wantonly: adv. In a deliberate, cruel, or immoral way, without motive or provocation, and with a reckless disregard for justice or consequences.
welfare: n. The general health, happiness, and prosperity of a person or group; it can also refer to statutory procedures or social efforts designed to promote the basic physical and material well-being of people in need.
whence: adv. An adverb meaning 'from what place, source, or cause'.
woefully: adv. In a manner that is extremely bad, inadequate, or regrettable.
yield: verb, noun. (noun) The full amount of an agricultural or industrial product; (verb) to produce or provide a natural product or a result; to give way to demands or pressure.
